constructs.name: lipid_burden

constructs.name: glycemic_control

constructs.name: arterial_pressure

constructs.name: renal_function

constructs.name: medication_adherence
constructs.description: Prescription fill rate and treatment compliance across all prescribed medications

edges.description: Atherogenic lipids accelerate coronary and carotid atherosclerosis
Elevated blood pressure increases cardiac workload and vascular damage
Poor glycemic control drives micro- and macrovascular complications
Declining kidney function is an independent cardiovascular risk factor
Atorvastatin inhibits HMG-CoA reductase, reducing hepatic LDL synthesis
Ramipril and amlodipine reduce systemic vascular resistance
Metformin improves hepatic insulin sensitivity and reduces gluconeogenesis
Sustained hypertension causes glomerular hyperfiltration injury
Worsening cardiovascular state feeds back into vascular stiffness

messages.content: You are a clinical epidemiologist specializing in cardiometabolic causal inference...
Research question: What factors drive this patient's cardiovascular risk, given 3 years of Doctolib medical records including prescriptions, lab results, and vital signs?
I'll construct a latent causal model for this patient's cardiovascular risk trajectory based on their clinical history.
messages.reasoning: Patient has T2DM, hypertension, hypercholesterolemia. Key latent constructs: lipid burden (statin-modifiable), glycemic control (metformin-modifiable), arterial pressure (ACE-i + CCB modifiable), renal function (downstream of BP and glucose), and overall CV risk as the outcome. Medication adherence is exogenous.

messages.content: The latent model captures 6 constructs and 9 directed edges. The contemporaneous subgraph is acyclic; feedback between CV risk and arterial pressure is modeled via lagged edges.

context: Stage 1a proposes a latent causal model from the patient’s clinical history. Constructs represent physiological subsystems relevant to cardiovascular risk in a type 2 diabetes patient on polypharmacy.
